audit_items.proof_trace: The function verifies a Merkle proof for sidecar.KzgCommitments without validating that these commitments match the actual commitments in the signed block body. An attacker can provide arbitrary KzgCommitments with a valid proof, bypassing the binding requirement.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker crafts a data column sidecar with a legitimate SignedBlockHeader but substitutes malicious KzgCommitments (M1,M2,M3) different from the actual block body commitments (C1,C2,C3). The attacker computes a valid Merkle proof for the malicious commitments. Verification passes because the proof structurally validates the malicious commitments, but never checks they match the real block body.
